The PQ’s victory was both impressive and disappointing. The party added 56 seats to its roster and more than doubled its vote share compared with the 2022 election, giving it its first taste of power in 14 years. The explosive hit the key airport moments before a plane was due to land. The British ambassador to Yemen, Abda Sharif, said the attack could have endangered thousands of people. It forced the flight – from Cairo – to be diverted to Jeddah and led to a review about the safety of flights in Aden.

events.title: ‘Palestinians will bear the cost’: UK consulate in East Jerusalem prepares to shut its doors
events.summary:
Forced closure marks low point in UK-Israeli relations, with reports UK is considering retaliatory expulsion of Israeli diplomats from London

The UK consulate in East Jerusalem gave few signs it was at the centre of a geopolitical controversy this week, with little movement around the high-walled building save the fluttering of the union jack and the occasional car exiting the compound.

The mission is to shut its doors on Thursday after Israel ordered its closure in response to a UK ban on trade with illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank and sanctions on those who help build or finance them.

events.title: Israeli settlers beat press photographer as soldiers watch in West Bank
events.summary:
Jaafar Ashtiyeh was covering violence against olive farmers when settlers set upon him with the butts of their rifles

Armed Israeli settlers beat a photographer in the presence of Israeli soldiers, hospitalising him, as he covered worsening settler violence against olive farmers in the occupied West Bank.

Jaafar Ashtiyeh, a 58-year-old veteran photographer for Agence France-Presse in Palestine, was assaulted by a group of settlers, who beat him with the butts of their rifles, despite him being marked as press. He was assaulted in view of about a dozen armed Israeli soldiers.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘All I want to do is cry’: trauma of 7 October survivors three years after the attacks
events.summary:
Israeli communities shattered by Hamas massacres are torn between rebuilding their lives and remembering lost friends and relatives

Keith Siegel spent many of his long hours in Hamas captivity in Gaza etching everything that happened after 7 October 2023 into his memory. For 484 days, he recited to himself every place he was held, the dates he was moved and every attack or humiliation he endured or witnessed.

He aimed to store intelligence that could help Israeli forces free other hostages if he was released, to keep track of time as the days slid by and be able to tell his family what happened to him. Now his body is free, but he cannot loosen those memories.

Continue reading...

events.title: Supporters of Imran Khan start march on locked-down Islamabad
events.summary:
Pakistani authorities insist marchers calling for former PM to be released from jail will not reach the capital

Imran Khan’s supporters have begun a march to Islamabad to demand his release from jail after efforts by the government to halt the protest failed.

The march began in the former prime minister’s stronghold province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in north-west Pakistan on Sunday, according to leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.

Continue reading...

events.title: India’s Cockroach movement launches new protests over changes to voter roll
events.summary:
Thousands gather in Mumbai with heavy police presence as concerns mount that millions will be denied voting rights

India’s youth-led Cockroach movement kicked off more nationwide protests on Friday as thousands of people gathered in Mumbai, amid mounting concerns that millions of citizens are being unfairly stripped of their vote.

The movement, which calls itself the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) and has massive support among the country’s gen Zs, returned to the streets to demand the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.

events.title: Eastern Spain braces for torrential rain and flooding
events.summary:
Up to 300mm of rain could fall in places, while extreme downpours bring landslides and deaths in Nepal

Torrential rain and potentially damaging flooding are forecast in eastern Spain over the coming days, as cold upper air moves over the warm, humid surface air of the Mediterranean Sea, fuelling violent, slow-moving thunderstorms near Spain’s east coast. The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.

Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, are most at risk. Valencia has experienced several damaging floods in recent years. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘I was fighting for my life’: Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls flydubai cockpit attack
events.summary:
Smit Machchhar says in video call with Indian PM that he realised if he did not get up ‘passengers would lose their lives’

The Indian pilot who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv said his faith and his desire to save his passengers allowed him to make a “last push” to open the cockpit door as he fought for his life.

Capt Smit Machchhar, who was recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, described to India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, how he helped save the plane and its more than 170 passengers.

Continue reading...

events.title: British Sikh activist released from Delhi jail after nine-year detention
events.summary:
Indian government issued with warning it would be in contempt of court if it failed to release Jagtar Singh Johal

The British Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal has been released from a Delhi prison after the Indian high court warned the government it would be found in contempt of court if it continued to attempt to keep him in jail despite an 18 September court order releasing him on bail. Johal has been incarcerated for nine years without any full trial.

The court order was issued after Johal’s lawyers issued a writ of habeas corpus alleging he was being detained against the express direction of the court.

events.title: Teenager becomes first person to have testicular tissue transplant in UK
events.summary:
Operation on 19-year-old who had no sperm after chemotherapy offers hope of preserving children’s fertility after cancer treatment

Surgeons have performed the first testicular tissue transplant on a teenager in the UK, offering hope that boys left infertile by chemotherapy could one day have biological children.

The 19-year-old had his tissue removed and frozen three years ago before undergoing treatment for a serious blood disorder. He said he was “incredibly grateful” to the medical team behind the pioneering procedure, which represents a potential breakthrough for male fertility preservation.

events.title: Bendy elm still standing against all odds crowned UK tree of the year
events.summary:
Hundred-and-fifty-year-old Wych elm in Newcastle, Co Down has grown sideways owing to strong winds

The “astonishing and bizarre” Bendy Tree in Northern Ireland has been crowned the winner of this year’s tree of the year competition.

The wych elm tree, located in Newcastle, County Down, owes its name to its near horizontal trunk, which has grown sideways owing to the strong seaside winds coming off the Irish Sea.

events.title: Family of student who took his own life say university ‘will be held to account’
events.summary:
Ethan Scott Brown died after being wrongly told he would not be eligible to graduate from the University of Glasgow

The family of a student who took his own life after being wrongly told he would not be eligible to graduate have said the University of Glasgow “will be held to account”.

Ethan Scott Brown, 23, was due to graduate in December 2024 after studying geography.

events.title: Labour Send changes at risk as parents rush to secure support, say experts
events.summary:
Overhaul of special education in England could unravel, thinktank finds, because of ‘use it before you lose it’ dynamic

Labour’s flagship changes to special education in England are at risk of unravelling because parents are rushing to secure support for their children before the system changes, new analysis has found.

The Institute for Government (IfG) thinktank says the government’s plans to largely replace education, health and care plans (EHCPs) in England with more widespread support in mainstream schools may be too optimistic and take longer to complete than its 2030 timeline.

events.title: Two men serving indefinite jail sentences freed after two decades
events.summary:
Convicted pair, plus third man released in August, have IPPs replaced after serving much longer than minimum terms

Two men jailed with indefinite sentences for public protection (IPPs) have been freed after each serving about two decades in custody despite receiving minimum terms of two years or less.

A high court judge and a magistrate hearing an appeal after a review by the Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC) told Luke Ings and Liam Bennett they would be freed, and also replaced an indeterminate sentence given to a third man, James Ward.

At least half a dozen demonstrators interrupted the US president during his remarks in San Antonio, with some led away by police. One was physically assaulted by an older Trump supporter as he tried to leave the arena.

events.summary:

Tonight, we’ll have another set of midterm debates. In Iowa, we’ll see the Republican nominee for US Senate, Ashley Hinson, face off against Democrat Josh Turek, a state representative and Paralympian at 8pm ET.

The race has become one of the most competitive of this cycle, despite the fact a Democrat hasn’t won a Senate election in the Hawkeye state since 2008. events.title: Texas kills man in first US execution since botched lethal injection of Christa Pike
events.summary:
Jamaal Howard, 46, executed by fatal dose of pentobarbital after lawyers’ bid for stay had been denied

A Texas man was put to death Wednesday in the first US execution since the botched lethal injection of Christa Pike in Tennessee last week.

Jamaal Howard, 46, was pronounced dead at 8.03pm after receiving a fatal dose of pentobarbital, a sedative, at the state prison in Huntsville.

events.title: Margaret Hamilton, trailblazer whose software powered Apollo 11 moon landing, dies at 90
events.summary:
MIT computer scientist led development of software for moon mission and earned Presidential Medal of Freedom

Margaret Hamilton, the computer pioneer whose software powered the first moon landing, has died, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) announced on Wednesday. She was 90.

In an era before titles such as software engineer and computer scientist became mainstream, Hamilton, who died on 30 September, learned to program under the tutelage of a renowned MIT meteorologist.

events.title: Patricia Krenwinkel, former Manson follower, granted parole for third time
events.summary:
The 78-year-old has spent nearly six decades in prison and California governor has overturned last two parole grants

Patricia Krenwinkel, a former Charles Manson follower, was granted parole on Tuesday after nearly six decades in prison for her role in the infamous Tate-LaBianca murders in Los Angeles.

This is the third time that Krenwinkel, 78, has been approved for release by California’s board of parole hearings. After both of her last two parole grants, Gavin Newsom, California’s governor, reversed the parole board’s decisions and denied her freedom, and Krenwinkel’s attorneys are now urging the Democrat to allow this latest ruling to stand.

events.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
events.summary: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.

events.title: Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
events.summary: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

events.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
events.summary: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.

events.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
events.summary: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

events.title: Germany news: Volkswagen ends collective wage agreements
events.summary: In an effort to cut costs, automaker Volkswagen terminated most of its collective wage agreements in Germany. This could reignite disputes with employee representatives.

events.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
events.summary: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.

events.title: South Park satirist pushes for accountability in Cornell gang-rape lawsuit
events.summary: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.

events.title: Global trade weathers Iran, Ukraine and Trump's tariffs
events.summary: Over the past six years, COVID, two wars and Donald Trump's tariffs have shaken world trade. With globalization already stalling, is this a temporary shock or the start of a great reversal?

events.title: AI: Concern as Germany plans to double data center capacity
events.summary: Germany is rewriting the rules to attract data center investment from AI companies. But local communities are becoming increasingly skeptical.

events.title: Spain grows fruit and vegetables for Europe, but it's running out of water
events.summary: Spain's southern coast produces up to 25% of Europe's fruit and vegetables. But amid intensive farming, climate change and illegal wells, the water it takes to grow them is drying up.

events.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?
events.summary: Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty of major financial rule breaches. What does this mean for German football?

events.title: Germany news: COVID vaccine maker BioNTech to close 3 sites
events.summary: COVID-19 vaccine maker BioNTech is to close three sites in Germany after efforts to find buyers failed. Meanwhile, Rhine water levels have fallen to record lows after an unusually dry September. DW has more.

events.title: Diesel prices are surging putting further pressure on Europe
events.summary: Trucks, farms and industry are powered with diesel. Now prices are soaring due to refinery disruptions, supply shortages and geopolitical tensions. A potential US export ban could make Europe's diesel crunch even worse.

events.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?
events.summary: After defeat to Greece, Jürgen Klopp faces the first real test of his tenure as coach of Germany's national men's football team. Can his charisma alone push this group forward?

events.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
events.summary: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip.

events.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
events.summary: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.

events.title: Germany news: Are Germans giving up their beloved meat and sausages?
events.summary: Germans used to be all about sausages and meat. While those do remain popular, things seem to be slowly changing. There also are new insights into the economic side of East Germany's espionage DW has more.

events.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
events.summary: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

events.title: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
events.summary: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.

events.title: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
events.summary: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.

events.title: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
events.summary: A late Netherlands goal denied Jürgen Klopp a win in his first match as Germany coach. The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund boss has big ambitions, but the game showed he's going to need more time to achieve them.

events.title: Three-way battle for power in world chess: Who will be elected FIDE president in Samarkand?
events.summary: The era of Russian presidents is coming to an end at the World Chess Federation (FIDE). Two Germans and one Kazakh are up for election. Among the issues at play are money, Kremlin influence, and unanswered questions.

events.title: After several difficult years, economists now expect German economy to grow
events.summary: Germany's economy is growing again, but recovery remains on shaky ground. High government spending is keeping the economy afloat, while energy prices, a shortage of skilled workers and debt continue to weigh on it.

events.title: Political psychology: Why extremist parties are thriving and what democratic politicians can do against it
events.summary: Far-right and far-left parties are celebrating success after success, leaving moderate politicians in the dust and worrying many Germans. Political psychology helps us understand what's behind growing polarization.

events.title: Could flattering AI make humanity turn on itself?
events.summary: A study shows chatbots mirror users' politics, part of a broader tendency known as AI sycophancy. Researchers fear this could deepen polarization.

events.title: Germany news: Berlin officially withdraws Olympics bid
events.summary: Berlin's decision to withdraw its Olympic bid means that only Munich and the western Rhine/Ruhr region are left in the running as potential Olympic hosts. DW has more.

events.title: Could a Left Party government in Berlin expropriate large real estate companies?
events.summary: The socialist Left Party won the Berlin election partly on the promise to implement the city's 2021 expropriation referendum as a way to solve the city's rent crisis. But can it really happen?

events.title: China's 13-year-old swimming star raises questions on child athletes
events.summary: Three gold medals and three Asian Games records have catapulted China's Yu Zidi, 13, into the sporting spotlight. She is far from the first teen prodigy, but should teens be competing at elite level?

events.title: Munich and Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr – Germany's two remaining Olympic candidates
events.summary: Munich or the Cologne-Rhine-Ruhr region? Germany aims to host the Olympic Games again. Just two candidates are left after Berlin pulled out at the last minute.

events.title: El Nino explained: How the weather pattern affects hurricanes and tropical storms
events.summary: From drought to major floods and extreme heat, El Nino will have a huge impact on the world's weather. In the Atlantic, it could mean a season without hurricanes.

events.title: China's new travel rules unsettle tech giants and talent
events.summary: Beijing is locking the gates to stop expertise and capital in strategic industries from fleeing. The country accused of industrial-scale intellectual property theft now fears the West will take its own.

events.title: Living in the shadow of LA's hidden oil wells
events.summary: Many lifelong residents of Los Angeles have health impacts from growing up close to oil extraction. Now, the city is trying to close down the worst offenders, but it's an enormous task.

events.title: Could we see MMA at the Olympics?
events.summary: Mixed martial arts has made its debut at the Asian Games this week. It takes the sport closer to the Olympics, but there are doubts about the next step — and the influence of the popular and lucrative UFC.

events.title: Male infertility is 'grossly underreported'
events.summary: It's not all on women anymore — doctors do test men for sperm count and motility. But still too few men get checked, possibly due to a misconception that a healthy sex life means healthy sperm. Spoiler: It doesn't.

events.title: Will Germany have enough gas this winter amid energy supply crunch?
events.summary: Germany's gas storage sites are far less full than in recent years. Officials say supplies are secure, but analysts warn that a cold winter or import disruptions could push prices higher. So how secure is the supply?

events.title: Princess Diana's brother makes explosive claims about royals in new memoir
events.summary: Here are some of the key revelations from Charles Earl Spencer's highly anticipated memoir "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." It has already provoked Buckingham Palace to react.

events.title: Germany's car crisis: Can the 35-hour workweek survive?
events.summary: German carmakers want employees to work 40 hours instead of the current 35 without extra pay, arguing it would improve competitiveness. Unions strongly oppose the proposal and view it as an attack on workers' rights.

events.title: Germany faces energy tax losses as EV sales rise
events.summary: The rapid shift to electric vehicles in Germany is cutting fuel tax revenue for the government. As EV sales surge, policymakers face growing pressure to find new ways to fund roads and transportation infrastructure.

events.title: Summer of 2026 broke records in Europe, and caused deaths

events.title: Oktoberfest 2026: Everything you need to know

events.title: Rebels, workers, radicals: The making of 'Red Berlin'
events.summary: Bloody May, student sit-ins and the squatter movement: Berlin has long been a hotbed for working-class organizing and radical left-wing politics.

events.title: Women's football in Germany booming, but still much to do
events.summary: Women's football is growing rapidly, particularly in Germany. Nevertheless, equal pay and investment remain major talking points.

events.summary: As war disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, satellite images reveal that oil is spreading toward protected coral reefs and mangrove forests.

events.title: Dual citizenship means Germany now in competition for talent
events.summary: Coach Jürgen Klopp has named several players to his first Germany squad who are eligible to play for other countries. Some still aren't committed to playing for thje national team long-term.

events.title: Beethoven and Andy Warhol: Rebel icons on show in Bonn
events.summary: The new exhibition "Beethoven by Warhol" at the Beethoven House in Bonn presents the pop artist's late masterpiece: a picture of Ludwig van Beethoven. The exhibition shares the story of the work with the public.

events.title: VAR's mission creep a problem for football
events.summary: After a decade of use, questions around VAR in football are louder than ever. Has the technology strayed too far from its remit?

events.title: Alexander Ovechkin backs Putin party in campaign video
events.summary: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

events.summary: Jürgen Klopp, Germany's new head coach, says he wants his team to reclaim pride in being German after recent political developments.

events.summary: Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

events.summary: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

events.title: How climate change worsened Nepal's deadly mountain collapse
events.summary: A glacier and rock collapse in Nepal killed nearly 1,400 people and left thousands missing. Scientists say decades of warming helped set the disaster in motion.

events.title: Global Gender Gap Report: Women's hard-won gains 'fragile'
events.summary: Two decades of progress toward gender parity is at risk as women's political representation declines, according to a new World Economic Forum report. At the current pace, the remaining gap could take 120 years to close.

events.title: German drama 'Blindspot Berlin' revisits 2016 Christmas market attack
events.summary: A decade after the terrorist attack on a Berlin Christmas market, a new German miniseries looks into the institutional failures that allowed the deadly truck rampage to happen.

events.title: How extreme heat is hitting wallets
events.summary: Heat waves, wildfires and floods have cascading economic impacts, causing incomes to decline and the price of basic goods to rise. The trend will escalate as temperatures continue to increase.

events.title: Spanish scientists find first evidence of Diplodocus dinosaur in Europe
events.summary: Paleontologists in Spain say they have found the first evidence of the long-necked Diplodocus genus of dinosaur outside of North America. They found bones at the rich La Tejeria fossil site in Teruel in eastern Spain.

events.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
events.summary: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?

events.title: Why AI researchers warn humanity could face extinction
events.summary: Could artificial intelligence pose an existential threat to humanity? Some leading researchers are warning against an unregulated race toward AI superintelligence.

events.title: Iran and US: Two countries and the pistachio between them
events.summary: The pistachios sold across the United States have a surprising history: California's trees trace their roots to Iran. Now, both regions face the same threat — their farmland is sinking as groundwater disappears.

events.title: Africa's richest man Dangote's IPO out of reach in Nigeria
events.summary: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?

events.title: The Crusades: How a medieval holy war still shapes politics
events.summary: In 1095, the Catholic Church launched the Crusades: wars that left millions dead and whose legacy still shapes political and ideological conflicts.

events.title: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
events.summary: Iran is shifting trade toward northern ports and land routes as its southern shipping faces a US blockade. Analysts say the corridors can keep essential goods moving, but cannot replace maritime trade.

events.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
events.summary: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

events.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Nino events intensifying?
events.summary: Records show that El Nino events have been frequent and often extreme over the past few decades. Is this normal? Or is it the result of climate change? Corals can give us a clear indication.

events.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn
events.summary: The BRICS summit 2026 takes place in Delhi this weekend. Unlike last year, Putin and Xi are expected to attend. Can India keep the expanded bloc united?

events.title: The 'end of an era' as Goethe-Institut in Russia closes
events.summary: The Goethe-Institut was one of the last German institutions still operating in Russia. However, following Moscow's decision to close its offices, all employees will have to stop working by September 13.

events.title: How Celine Dion became a pop culture icon across generations
events.summary: As the global star kicks off her anticipated Paris residency, here's how Celine Dion managed to gain younger followers while keeping her loyal older fans.

events.title: How Belarusians still find hope in a silenced country
events.summary: The documentary "Letters from the Silenced Country" depicts the ongoing repression under the authoritarian regime. Director Andrei Kutsila talked to DW ahead of the film's Venice premiere.

events.title: Why we're still looking for dark matter
events.summary: When physicists said they may have spotted evidence of dark matter almost 100 years after it was proposed as a theory, the internet lit up. Here's why we're searching for the thing that holds everything else together.

events.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers but not peace
events.summary: Twenty-five years after 9/11, conspiracy theories about the terrorist attacks persist. But even as an attempt to make sense of a tragedy, psychologists say the benefit in conspiracy ideation or belief is short-lived.

events.title: The billion-euro trade driving Europe's eels to extinction
events.summary: Traffickers are making big bucks smuggling millions of critically endangered eels across continents, using suitcases on planes and legal loopholes to deliver them to dinnerplates. Where are the smuggling hotspots?

events.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: What's behind the hype?
events.summary: The exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum is eagerly anticipated across the UK, as the medieval masterpiece is considered by many to be a symbol of the country's identity.

events.title: Live: French high school, university students call for fresh protests as funding demands grow
events.summary: French high school and university students were called out to protest again on Thursday, two days after a large turnout demanding more funding, as the government made a series of conciliatory gestures aimed at ending the crisis. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.

events.title: Saudi Arabia strikes back after deadly Houthi attacks on airports
events.summary: Saudi authorities said Wednesday three people were killed and 36 wounded in attacks on Abha and Riyadh’s King Khalid international airports claimed by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed the ballistic missile launch platform used to attack Riyadh, as fighting with the Houthis intensified across the region.

events.title: DNC sues Trump administration over taxpayer-funded TV ads promoting president
events.summary: The Democratic National Committee sued President Donald Trump’s administration on Wednesday over taxpayer-funded television ads promoting his political message, alleging illegal government propaganda. The lawsuit seeks to halt federal funding for the ads, which have cost more than $12 million to air ahead of November’s midterm elections, according to AdImpact.

events.title: No longer the same Israel? October 7th and the future of the Jewish State
events.summary: For now, it's still Benjamin Netanyahu’s Israel. In 2023, in the immediate aftermath of the country’s worst day of bloodshed in its history, pundits predicted the quick demise of the right wing prime minister. On this the third anniversary of the October Seventh attacks, Israel’s still not reckoned with the security failures on the day, the root causes of the Hamas-led terror attack, the brutal war of vengeance that followed and most of all, Netanyahu’s still prime minister with a fair shot at re-election. Even if the Likud leader’s voted out on October 27th, his most serious general election rivals don't exactly advocate for a radical break when it comes to the Palestinians.

events.title: Thousands protest Flavio Bolsonaro, fearing far-right return in Brazil
events.summary: Thousands of people joined a student march in downtown Rio de Janeiro on Wednesday to protest against Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of Brazil's October 25 presidential runoff. Bolsonaro led Sunday's first-round vote, prompting demonstrators to rally behind incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and oppose the far right's return to power.

events.title: Israel marks three years since October 7 attack ahead of elections
events.summary: Israel marked the third anniversary of Hamas’s October 7 attack on Wednesday with silent tributes and renewed strikes on Gaza as political debate intensified ahead of elections. Families gathered at the Nova festival site and Kfar Aza kibbutz. Gaza officials said strikes killed five people despite a year-old ceasefire agreement.

events.title: UN health agency wants more details from Russia on suspected pneumonic plague case
events.summary: A top official with the World Health Organization said Wednesday it doesn’t know how a lab worker in Siberia died, and she urged Russia to provide more information about a case that prompted global concerns about suspected pneumonic plague. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis reports.

events.title: France suspends stun grenade use at student protests after pupil loses hand
events.summary: France has suspended the use of stun grenades by police at student-led demonstrations, the interior minister said Wednesday, as allegations of police brutality mounted after days of sometimes violent demonstrations across the country. Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across France on Tuesday demanding better conditions in high schools. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis reports.

events.title: French PM vows to address debt despite student protests
events.summary: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has tried to calm both student protesters and jittery bond markets. In an address to the nation, Lecornu stressed that the education ministry had not seen any cuts in last week's budget proposal, but insisted the government must cut its public deficit to 5%. There are growing concerns about France's spending and debt, with the IMF urging the country to "get your house in order." Lecornu also confirmed the release of 10 million barrels of diesel fuel.

events.title: Africa joins the data center backlash
events.summary: In tonight's edition, witnesses say Eritrean troops have moved into Ethiopia's Tigray region, but Asmara rejects the reports. Also, the African Union launches the Africa Credit Rating Agency, aiming to assess the financial health of African states and companies. And South African civil society is pushing back against the expansion of data centres  that require vast amounts of electricity, water and land.

events.title: France schools protests: more than 6,000 arrested since start of demonstrations
events.summary: After more than two weeks of high school protests across France, police have arrested a total of 6,100 individuals, the majority of whom are minors who, until now, had no previous criminal record. So, what has happend to these students, and what lies ahead for them? FRANCE 24's Caitlin Brown has more.

events.title: Evicted pensioner who sparked Spain housing protests dies: tenant union
events.summary: Maricarmen ​Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction sparked housing ​protests in Spain, has died, Madrid's tenants' union said on Wednesday. Abascal's eviction sparked a series of ​protests ‌across Spain in the past couple ⁠of weeks, including activists camping on one of Madrid's main ‌squares, and calls for tackling a ⁠mounting housing crisis. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.

events.title: 'It's still unclear whether Netanyahu will pay for what happened during his time in office'
events.summary: As Israel marks the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, questions linger about the warnings Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu received about them. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Ayala Panievsky, Lecturer at City University of London and author of The New Censorship, explains that the allegations in the run-up to the elections "are very damaging for Netanyahu but there are some factors mitigating the risk for him", including a fragmented opposition as well as the control of major media.

events.title: White House promotes 'Trump TV' with an AI-altered photo
events.summary: The White House has promoted “Trump TV” using an AI-altered photo of passengers apparently watching the president’s new streaming channel. But the image was originally posted online in February 2023, showing passengers watching the NFL Super Bowl, with one watching the film “Hitch”. The original photo was modified using AI to make it appear the passengers were watching Trump TV. The post did not disclose that the image had been altered. Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

events.title: Evicted pensioner Maricarmen Abascal, heart of Spain's housing protests, dies
events.summary: Maricarmen ​Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction sparked housing ​protests in Spain, has died, Madrid's tenants' union said on Wednesday. Massive protests following Abascal's eviction spiralled into a political crisis, eventually leading Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call a snap election.

events.title: Trump says 'we don't think' Russian plague is bio-weapon
events.summary: US President Donald Trump said Wednesday that the death of a Russian plague laboratory worker did not appear to be linked to a biological weapon. "We don't think so. We're going to find out soon enough, but we don't think so," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked if a "bio-weapon" was involved. Russia warned earlier against "false" information as reports emerged of a second suspected case. The US and UN have urged Russia to be more transparent. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

events.title: 'Resilience' of Israelis as they mourn the loss of loved ones and 'the sense that we can be safe'
events.summary: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Dr. Danny Brom, Founding Director of METIV, the Israel Psychotrauma Center in Jerusalem. According to Dr. Brom, as Israelis and Jewish people around the world continue to mourn the largest loss of Jewish life on a single day since the Holocaust, their fundamental sense of collective security has also been shattered. What strikes him, however, is the resilience that exists alongside the grieving. How can individuals, communities and society rebuild a sense of safety without allowing fear to dictate the future? Yet, as Dr. Brom observes, “the war is still going on,” while political leaders speak of pursuing “the ultimate victory, which no one really knows what that is.”

events.title: France summons Iranian ambassador over 'disinformation' on student protests
events.summary: The French foreign ministry on Wednesday summoned the Iranian ambassador to protest against a "disinformation campaign conducted by the Iranian authorities" over the student protests that have rocked France. The move came a day after Tehran summoned the French ambassador over the treatment of protesters in France.

events.title: France suspends the use of stun grenades after student protester loses hand
events.summary: The French ​government said Wednesday it would suspend the use of stun grenades in its attempts to manage the student protests now roiling the country after a 15-year-old boy had his hand blown off during a clash with riot police.

events.title: What France's student protesters want – and what the government is offering
events.summary: Staff shortages, rats in the corridors, and a university admissions system that feels like a lottery: As protests sweep France, high school students have drawn up a list of demands to deal with these and other issues. events.title: Scars from Oct. 7 fuel deep divisions over Netanyahu ahead of Israeli election
events.summary: As Israel gears up for its first elections since Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his opponents are putting it at the heart of their campaigns. events.title: Russian strikes on Ukrainian cities kill at least 21 in a major attack that Kyiv saw coming
events.summary: Without ammunition for its U.S.-made Patriot air defense systems, Ukraine can’t stop Russian ballistic weapons.

events.title: Russia says no plague found in contacts of Siberian lab worker who died
events.summary: News that a female staffer had died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin last week has spread fears worldwide.

events.summary: Jesse Van Rootselaar, 18, killed her mother and stepbrother and then five students and a teacher at a secondary school in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, in February.

events.summary: The suspect was being questioned by investigators in the United Arab Emirates.

events.title: Iranian drone threat prompted U.S. to remove bombers from British base, officials say
events.summary: The bombers at RAF Fairford “have been re-deployed to their home stations in the United States,” a Pentagon official told NBC News.

events.title: BA flight to Chicago drops 28,000 feet, returns to London
events.summary: About 30 minutes into its journey, the aircraft dropped from 36,000 feet to 9,000 feet in around seven minutes, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware.

events.title: 200 people enter medical observation after worker at Russian anti-plague lab dies
events.summary: The female staffer at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East died from a “pneumonia of undetermined” origin last week, according to a regional governor.

events.title: Russia pounds Kyiv during German chancellor’s visit in a new escalation
events.summary: Germany’s foreign intel chief warns it could become embroiled in a conflict with Russia as Moscow steps up its “shadow war” against European democracies.

events.title: Early indications suggest Flydubai co-pilot acted alone in attack, officials say
events.summary: Officials cautioned that the investigation remains in its early stages and that possible links to an organization or foreign government haven’t been definitively ruled out.

events.title: U.S. Marine arrested on suspicion of killing Japanese woman in Okinawa
events.summary: Japan’s Defense Ministry said it was “deeply outraged by the extremely brutal and heinous crime committed by a U.S. Marine.”

events.title: Flydubai pilot attacked captain with cockpit’s crash ax in attempted terrorist act, UAE official says
events.summary: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.

events.title: Two Iranian nationals charged over alleged terrorism plot targeting Jewish community in England
events.summary: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

events.title: Screaming, panicking, blood: Passengers detail horrifying Israel-bound flight
events.summary: It was too early to say why a pilot stabbed another on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

events.title: What we know about the cockpit stabbing on Israel-bound flight

events.title: Britain believes Iran was involved in incident near air base used by U.S., prime minister says
events.summary: Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorist offenses in the incident outside RAF Fairford. Iran had denied any involvement.

events.title: What we know about the pilot hailed as a hero for averting crash of Israel-bound plane
events.summary: He is being hailed around the world as a hero for helping stop a passenger plane bound for Israel from plunging into the ground, despite his own severe injuries.
